claims.statement: The scheduler graph is a single-node StateGraph (START -> launch -> END) registered as the `scheduler` assistant, and `_launch` deterministically routes each tick without invoking an LLM.

`_launch` routes named tasks to reconciliation, baby-sit, background-task monitoring, workspace refresh, session and agent cost refresh, thread feedback, and human-review deadline handlers; only an unrecognized or absent task uses `launch_scheduled_agent_run(schedule_id)`.

When a keyed scheduler tick lacks its required watch, thread, review request, or schedule key, `_launch` returns a `missing_*` status result rather than raising; exhausted transient sandbox attachment retries return `sandbox_unavailable`.

Dashboard-managed recurring agent schedules validate cron strings with normalize_cron_schedule, which requires a five-field expression and range-checks each field while supporting steps, ranges, and lists before storage.

Dashboard schedule definitions and their execution state use separate namespaces; launch_scheduled_agent_run loads a stored schedule and, when eligible, creates a fresh durable agent thread/run while separately recording last thread, run, trigger time, or pre-launch error.

reconcile_stale_runs is the durable-dispatch safety net: it paginates every `busy` thread, lists its `pending` runs, and cancels (action=interrupt) those older than max_age_seconds (default 1800s), so runs whose completion webhook never fired do not hold a thread busy forever.

The reconcile sweep wraps per-thread work in try/except so one bad thread never aborts the sweep, skips malformed timestamps, and returns counts of threads checked, stale runs found, and runs cancelled.

Session-cost refresh is a self-terminating chain of stateless delayed scheduler runs: successful Slack-correlated agent completion schedules an attempt, and run_session_cost_refresh updates the mapped Slack footer or retries transient pending results through a fixed five-delay budget.

Each baby-sit watch is a BabySitWatch persisted in the `baby_sit_watches` store keyed by lower-cased owner/repo#pr_number, binding the watch to the originating agent thread_id, head SHA/ref, GitHub App installation id, captured run_config, and a SourceContext.

A pull request may be watched from only one agent thread at a time: start_watch rejects a second thread that tries to watch an already-active PR, and carries over retry/dedupe state only when the head SHA is unchanged.

start_watch registers each watch's per-watch LangGraph cron via _ensure_watch_cron, which idempotently reuses an existing cron tagged kind=baby_sit_watch (deleting duplicates) or creates one, and rolls back the store row and partial cron if cron creation fails for a brand-new watch.

The per-watch baby_sit cron fires on the fixed */10 * * * * UTC schedule against the scheduler assistant; pending and duplicate evaluations return statuses without dispatching an agent run, so unchanged polling consumes no model tokens.

Signed GitHub CI webhooks trigger watch evaluation: the GitHub route verifies the X-Hub-Signature-256 HMAC before processing, and handle_ci_webhook ignores incomplete CI payloads, matches active watches by head SHA or branch, and de-duplicates by delivery_id.

Both the webhook trigger and the cron trigger funnel into serialized evaluation under a per-key, five-minute short-lived lock thread, so a concurrent trigger returns busy and cannot dispatch the same watch concurrently.

On a new head SHA _evaluate_watch resets retry_count and failure/alert dedupe keys; on a genuinely new failing state it dispatches a confidence-gated `/baby-sit --continue` run to the originating agent thread and removes the fingerprint if dispatch fails, while already-dispatched fingerprints are skipped.

Flaky reruns are capped per head SHA at MAX_RETRIES_PER_HEAD (3), and record_retry increments the durable retry count only for the owning unchanged-head watch while posting the flaky-CI alert only on the first occurrence of a given check/safe URL for that head via alert_keys dedupe.

Terminal baby-sit outcomes for blocked checks, retry exhaustion, or MAX_EVALUATION_ERRORS evaluation failures are posted to the originating source context when possible and otherwise fall back to a queued `/baby-sit --terminal` run on the originating thread, after which the watch is stopped.

The manage_baby_sit tool is the agent-facing surface for durable watches, requiring a canonical PR URL and executable thread; start verifies authentication, open PR head data, and App installation, while stop and record_retry operate only on a watch owned by the current thread.

background_tasks provides model-free completion monitoring: callback-capable launches and a per-thread every-minute cron reconcile task state, atomically claim unreported terminal tasks before enqueueing a notification, and remove monitor crons only after a fresh idle check or missing thread/sandbox.

schedule_thread_wakeup schedules a one-shot re-trigger of the current agent thread from 1 minute to 24 hours as a thread-bound cron against the `agent` assistant, with an end_time about 90 seconds after firing and selected configuration passthrough.

Thread wakeups are budget-limited to at most 10 between human messages, keyed to the latest human-message generation so the budget resets on a new human message but not on system-kind messages; the budget is recorded before cron creation.

Because a fired wakeup cron's row is never deleted by firing, schedule_thread_wakeup opportunistically purges fully paginated expired `thread_wakeup` crons matched conservatively on kind plus a past end_time before creating a new one.

The baby-sit skill instructs cloud runs to use the durable manage_baby_sit watch (webhook plus 10-minute token-free fallback) while local/desktop runs instead use a bounded foreground `gh pr checks --watch` loop and never call manage_baby_sit or schedule_thread_wakeup.

Agent-usage cost refresh uses the scheduler's `agent_cost` task to fetch a run-only LangSmith cost and persist it to the invocation usage record; missing data or retrieval/persistence failures can advance only through the same fixed five-delay retry budget.

The purge_wakeup_crons operational script supports a dry run and deletion mode for expired `thread_wakeup` crons, resolving the deployment URL from `--url` or `LANGGRAPH_URL` and credentials from `LANGGRAPH_API_KEY` or `LANGSMITH_API_KEY`.
Focused tests cover scheduler compatibility and failure behavior, baby-sit lifecycle/concurrency/deduplication/readiness, and wakeup validation, configuration, limits, concurrency, and cleanup.

The scheduler routes `thread_feedback` delayed runs to a feedback handler that rechecks the saved feedback record, recent activity, and quiet period under a thread lock; it defers itself until due and only then marks and posts a ready prompt.

Workspace refresh ticks accept current `workspace_refresh` and legacy `environment_refresh` task names, invoke a full or update snapshot rebuild, and can sweep every workspace with a setup script when no slug is supplied.

A daily full workspace-refresh cron is staggered deterministically between 03:00 and 05:59 UTC; refresh captures a snapshot only after every required script succeeds, preserves the previous snapshot on failure, and releases its builder sandbox.

Baby-sit declares a PR ready only after all reported checks are terminal-successful and no branch-required check is absent; it then dispatches a ready continuation to the originating thread and stops the watch.
